text:
Above ponds, above valleys,
Above mountains and woods, seas and clouds,
Beyond suns, beyond ethers,
Beyond the boundary of starry spheres,


You move, my spirit, with all agility
And like a swimmer rapt in waves,
You joyfully furrow profound immensity
With unspeakable, virile delight.


Flee far from these morbid miasmas,
Rise to purify yourself in higher air
And drain, like a noble and divine liquor,
The clear light flooding limpid spaces.


Beyond weariness and deep griefs
That weigh upon misty life,
Happy is he who, with vigorous wings,
Can fling himself toward luminous, tranquil fields!


He whose thoughts, as if they were larks,
Lift their flight toward the morning sky—
He who soars above all, and effortlessly knows
The language of flowers and silent things!

translation.title: Elevation
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Baudelaire’s French original.
